claim: The nucleolus is a membrane-less organelle formed through liquid-liquid phase separation of its components from the surrounding nucleoplasm.
source: The nucleolus is a membrane-less organelle formed through liquid-liquid phase separation of its components from the surrounding nucleoplasm.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a foundational premise of the study.

claim: NPM1 integrates within the nucleolus via multivalent interactions with proteins containing arginine-rich linear motifs (R-motifs) and ribosomal RNA (rRNA).
source: Here, we show that nucleophosmin (NPM1) integrates within the nucleolus via a multi-modal mechanism involving multivalent interactions with proteins containing arginine-rich linear motifs (R-motifs) and ribosomal RNA (rRNA).
evidence: This is the main finding stated in the abstract, supported by multiple experiments throughout the manuscript.

claim: R-motifs are found in canonical nucleolar localization signals.
source: Importantly, these R-motifs are found in canonical nucleolar localization signals.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by bioinformatics analysis in the Discussion section.

claim: Multivalency of acidic tracts and folded nucleic acid binding domains, mediated by N-terminal domain oligomerization, are structural features required for phase separation of NPM1 with other nucleolar components in vitro.
source: We identify multivalency of acidic tracts and folded nucleic acid binding domains, mediated by N-terminal domain oligomerization, as structural features required for phase separation of NPM1 with other nucleolar components in vitro and for localization within mammalian nucleoli.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experiments with various NPM1 constructs shown in Figures 10-12.

claim: Multivalency of acidic tracts and folded nucleic acid binding domains are required for NPM1 localization within mammalian nucleoli.
source: We identify multivalency of acidic tracts and folded nucleic acid binding domains, mediated by N-terminal domain oligomerization, as structural features required for phase separation of NPM1 with other nucleolar components in vitro and for localization within mammalian nucleoli.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated through cell-based experiments in Figure 12.

claim: The nucleolus contains three substructures: the fibrillar centers (FCs), dense fibrillar component (DFC), and granular component (GC).
source: Nucleoli contain three substructures: the fibrillar centers (FCs) and dense fibrillar component (DFC) are engulfed in the granular component (GC) (Boisvert et al., 2007), which exhibits ATP-dependent liquid-like features (Brangwynne et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with citation to prior literature.

claim: The granular component (GC) of the nucleolus exhibits ATP-dependent liquid-like features.
source: Nucleoli contain three substructures: the fibrillar centers (FCs) and dense fibrillar component (DFC) are engulfed in the granular component (GC) (Boisvert et al., 2007), which exhibits ATP-dependent liquid-like features (Brangwynne et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with citation to Brangwynne et al., 2011.

claim: Ribosomal RNA (rRNA) genes are transcribed between the FC and DFC.
source: Ribosomal RNA (rRNA) genes are transcribed between the FC and DFC, and rRNAs are processed while migrating into the GC, wherein they assemble with ribosomal proteins to form pre-ribosomal particles (Boisvert et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with citation to prior literature.

claim: rRNAs are processed while migrating into the GC.
source: Ribosomal RNA (rRNA) genes are transcribed between the FC and DFC, and rRNAs are processed while migrating into the GC, wherein they assemble with ribosomal proteins to form pre-ribosomal particles (Boisvert et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with citation to prior literature.

claim: rRNAs assemble with ribosomal proteins to form pre-ribosomal particles in the GC.
source: Ribosomal RNA (rRNA) genes are transcribed between the FC and DFC, and rRNAs are processed while migrating into the GC, wherein they assemble with ribosomal proteins to form pre-ribosomal particles (Boisvert et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with citation to prior literature.

claim: NPM1 is a highly abundant marker of the GC.
source: Nucleophosmin (NPM1, also known as B23), a highly abundant marker of the GC, functions as a nucleolar chaperone and plays a role in cellular stress responses (Colombo et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with citation to prior literature.

claim: NPM1 functions as a nucleolar chaperone.
source: Nucleophosmin (NPM1, also known as B23), a highly abundant marker of the GC, functions as a nucleolar chaperone and plays a role in cellular stress responses (Colombo et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with citation to prior literature.

claim: NPM1 plays a role in cellular stress responses.
source: Nucleophosmin (NPM1, also known as B23), a highly abundant marker of the GC, functions as a nucleolar chaperone and plays a role in cellular stress responses (Colombo et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with citation to prior literature.

claim: The molecular basis of the GC's fluidity is unknown.
source: While appreciated (Brangwynne et al., 2011; Chen and Huang, 2001; Negi and Olson, 2006; Weber and Brangwynne, 2015), the molecular basis of the GC's fluidity is unknown.
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction as a knowledge gap.

claim: Npm1 loss is embryonic lethal in mice.
source: While Npm1 loss is embryonic lethal in mice, mouse fibroblasts derived from Npm1-/-/Trp53-/- embryos readily proliferate in culture (Colombo et al., 2005), indicating that NPM1 is dispensible for ribosome biogenesis.
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with citation to prior literature.

claim: Mouse fibroblasts derived from Npm1-/-/Trp53-/- embryos readily proliferate in culture.
source: While Npm1 loss is embryonic lethal in mice, mouse fibroblasts derived from Npm1-/-/Trp53-/- embryos readily proliferate in culture (Colombo et al., 2005), indicating that NPM1 is dispensible for ribosome biogenesis.
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with citation to prior literature.

claim: NPM1 is dispensible for ribosome biogenesis.
source: While Npm1 loss is embryonic lethal in mice, mouse fibroblasts derived from Npm1-/-/Trp53-/- embryos readily proliferate in culture (Colombo et al., 2005), indicating that NPM1 is dispensible for ribosome biogenesis.
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction as an inference from the cited study.

claim: NPM1 is known to influence ribosome biogenesis, genome stability and tumor suppression.
source: However, NPM1 is known to influence ribosome biogenesis, genome stability and tumor suppression (Lindstrom, 2011) and to participate in responses to cellular stresses, including DNA damage (Lee et al., 2005), chemotoxicity (Chan, 1992; Yao et al., 2010b), and oxidative stress (Paron et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with citations to prior literature.

claim: NPM1 participates in responses to DNA damage.
source: However, NPM1 is known to influence ribosome biogenesis, genome stability and tumor suppression (Lindstrom, 2011) and to participate in responses to cellular stresses, including DNA damage (Lee et al., 2005), chemotoxicity (Chan, 1992; Yao et al., 2010b), and oxidative stress (Paron et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with citation to prior literature.

claim: NPM1 participates in responses to chemotoxicity.
source: However, NPM1 is known to influence ribosome biogenesis, genome stability and tumor suppression (Lindstrom, 2011) and to participate in responses to cellular stresses, including DNA damage (Lee et al., 2005), chemotoxicity (Chan, 1992; Yao et al., 2010b), and oxidative stress (Paron et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with citations to prior literature.

claim: NPM1 participates in responses to oxidative stress.
source: However, NPM1 is known to influence ribosome biogenesis, genome stability and tumor suppression (Lindstrom, 2011) and to participate in responses to cellular stresses, including DNA damage (Lee et al., 2005), chemotoxicity (Chan, 1992; Yao et al., 2010b), and oxidative stress (Paron et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with citation to prior literature.

claim: NPM1 depletion is associated with disruption of nucleolar structure.
source: Furthermore, NPM1 depletion is associated with disruption of nucleolar structure (Holmberg Olausson et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with citation to prior literature.

claim: NPM1 participates in the organization of the liquid-like structure of the GC.
source: We propose that NPM1 participates in the organization of the liquid-like structure of the GC and consequently may actively participate in stress signal integration and transmission, thereby explaining its known roles in ribosome biogenesis, tumor suppression and other processes (Lindstrom, 2011).
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed in the Introduction based on the authors' reasoning.

claim: NPM1 interacts with a vast array of partners, many involved in ribosome biogenesis.
source: Accordingly, NPM1 interacts with a vast array of partners (http://thebiogrid.org/110929/summary/homo-sapiens/npm1.html), many involved in ribosome biogenesis, and controls the nucleolar localization of ribosomal (Lindstrom, 2012; Rosorius et al., 2000), viral (Duan et al., 2014; Fankhauser et al., 1991), and certain tumor suppressor proteins (Bertwistle et al., 2004), many of which engage the N-terminal oligomerization domain (OD) of NPM1 (Figure 1a) via arginine-rich short linear motifs (R-motifs) (Mitrea et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with citations to prior literature and databases.

claim: NPM1 controls the nucleolar localization of ribosomal, viral, and certain tumor suppressor proteins.
source: Accordingly, NPM1 interacts with a vast array of partners (http://thebiogrid.org/110929/summary/homo-sapiens/npm1.html), many involved in ribosome biogenesis, and controls the nucleolar localization of ribosomal (Lindstrom, 2012; Rosorius et al., 2000), viral (Duan et al., 2014; Fankhauser et al., 1991), and certain tumor suppressor proteins (Bertwistle et al., 2004), many of which engage the N-terminal oligomerization domain (OD) of NPM1 (Figure 1a) via arginine-rich short linear motifs (R-motifs) (Mitrea et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with citations to prior literature.

claim: Many NPM1 binding partners engage the N-terminal oligomerization domain (OD) of NPM1 via arginine-rich short linear motifs (R-motifs).
source: Accordingly, NPM1 interacts with a vast array of partners (http://thebiogrid.org/110929/summary/homo-sapiens/npm1.html), many involved in ribosome biogenesis, and controls the nucleolar localization of ribosomal (Lindstrom, 2012; Rosorius et al., 2000), viral (Duan et al., 2014; Fankhauser et al., 1991), and certain tumor suppressor proteins (Bertwistle et al., 2004), many of which engage the N-terminal oligomerization domain (OD) of NPM1 (Figure 1a) via arginine-rich short linear motifs (R-motifs) (Mitrea et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with citation to prior work by the authors.

claim: NPM1 binds nucleic acids (e.g., rRNA and DNA) through its C-terminal domain (nucleic acid binding domain, NBD).
source: Furthermore, NPM1 binds nucleic acids (e.g., rRNA and DNA) through its C-terminal domain (nucleic acid binding domain, NBD) (Wang et al., 1994).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with citation to prior literature.

claim: NPM1 undergoes liquid-liquid phase separation in the presence of proteins and RNA.
source: Here, we show that NPM1 undergoes liquid-liquid phase separation in the presence of two classes of nucleolar macromolecules: proteins and RNA.
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction as a main finding, supported by experiments in Figures 1, 8, and 9.

claim: 97% of NPM1-binding proteins exhibit at least one R-motif (RXn1R, where X is any amino acid and n1 ≤ 2).
source: Of 132 NPM1-binding proteins, 97% exhibited at least one R-motif (RXn1R, where X is any amino acid and n1 ≤ 2; Supplementary file 1) and 78.8% were annotated with GO terms indicating association with membrane-less organelles (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on bioinformatics analysis of NPM1 pull-down data.

claim: 78.8% of NPM1-binding proteins were annotated with GO terms indicating association with membrane-less organelles.
source: Of 132 NPM1-binding proteins, 97% exhibited at least one R-motif (RXn1R, where X is any amino acid and n1 ≤ 2; Supplementary file 1) and 78.8% were annotated with GO terms indicating association with membrane-less organelles (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on bioinformatics analysis.

claim: 73% of NPM1-binding proteins exhibited multiple R-motifs.
source: Amongst all 132 NPM1-binding proteins, 73% exhibited multiple R-motifs (Supplementary file 1); in contrast, only 44% of all human proteins exhibited multiple R-motifs (p<0.0001; Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on bioinformatics analysis.

claim: Only 44% of all human proteins exhibited multiple R-motifs.
source: Amongst all 132 NPM1-binding proteins, 73% exhibited multiple R-motifs (Supplementary file 1); in contrast, only 44% of all human proteins exhibited multiple R-motifs (p<0.0001; Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on bioinformatics analysis.

claim: Multivalent R-motifs are enriched in proteins that bind to NPM1.
source: Thus, multivalent R-motifs are enriched in proteins that bind to NPM1.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the statistical comparison (p<0.0001).

claim: R-motifs bind to a region of NPM1 which includes the OD and a short disordered region (residues 1–130; termed N130).
source: R-motifs bind to a region of NPM1 which includes the OD and a short disordered region (residues 1–130; termed N130; Figure 2a).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section, referencing Figure 2a.

claim: R-motif interactions with NPM1 engage two highly conserved acidic tracts, termed A1 (residues 34–39) and A2 (residues 120–130).
source: The interactions engage two highly conserved acidic tracts, termed A1 (residues 34–39) and A2 (residues 120–130), at the interface between monomer subunits and within the disordered region (Mitrea et al., 2014), respectively (Figure 2a).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citation to prior work and reference to Figure 2a.

claim: The A1 acidic tract is located at the interface between monomer subunits.
source: The interactions engage two highly conserved acidic tracts, termed A1 (residues 34–39) and A2 (residues 120–130), at the interface between monomer subunits and within the disordered region (Mitrea et al., 2014), respectively (Figure 2a).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citation to prior work.

claim: The A2 acidic tract is located within the disordered region.
source: The interactions engage two highly conserved acidic tracts, termed A1 (residues 34–39) and A2 (residues 120–130), at the interface between monomer subunits and within the disordered region (Mitrea et al., 2014), respectively (Figure 2a).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citation to prior work.

claim: The A tracts and the pentameric nature of N130 create multivalency within N130.
source: These A tracts and the pentameric nature create multivalency within N130.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an inference from the structural features.

claim: Multivalent interactions involving low complexity sequences cause assembly and phase separation of biopolymers within membrane-less organelles.
source: Multivalent interactions involving low complexity sequences cause assembly and phase separation of biopolymers within membrane-less organelles (Fromm et al., 2014; Li et al., 2012); therefore, we tested the ability of multivalent N130 and peptides containing multiple R-motifs derived from NPM1-binding proteins to undergo phase separation.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations to prior literature.

claim: Titration of four R-motif-containing peptides caused phase separation of N130 into liquid-like droplets.
source: Titration of four R-motif-containing peptides (Table 1) caused phase separation into liquid-like droplets (Figure 1b and Videos 1–4) at critical concentrations that varied with R-motif composition and affinity for N130 (Table 2 and Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1b and Videos 1-4.

claim: Critical concentrations for phase separation varied with R-motif composition and affinity for N130.
source: Titration of four R-motif-containing peptides (Table 1) caused phase separation into liquid-like droplets (Figure 1b and Videos 1–4) at critical concentrations that varied with R-motif composition and affinity for N130 (Table 2 and Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Table 2 and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: At 200 µM N130, phase separation with the divalent rpL5 peptide was observed when the rpL5:N130 ratio reached ~3:1.
source: At 200 µM N130, upon titration of the divalent rpL5 peptide, phase separation was observed when the rpL5:N130 ratio reached ~3:1 (Figure 2b).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2b.

claim: At 200 µM N130, phase separation was not observed upon titration of a monovalent R-motif peptide (rpL5-RA), even though it bound with lower affinity.
source: At the same N130 concentration, phase separation was not observed upon titration of a monovalent R-motif peptide (rpL5-RA; Figure 2b), even though it bound, albeit with lower affinity (Table 2 and Figure 1—figure supplement 1), confirming that R-motif multivalency is required for phase separation with N130.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2b, Table 2, and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: R-motif multivalency is required for phase separation with N130.
source: At the same N130 concentration, phase separation was not observed upon titration of a monovalent R-motif peptide (rpL5-RA; Figure 2b), even though it bound, albeit with lower affinity (Table 2 and Figure 1—figure supplement 1), confirming that R-motif multivalency is required for phase separation with N130.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the experimental data.

claim: A poly-R peptide, containing a single but longer R-motif with affinity similar to that of rpL5, failed to phase separate with N130.
source: The inability to phase separate was not due to reduced binding affinity (rather than loss of multivalency); a poly-R peptide, containing a single but longer R-motif, with affinity similar to that of rpL5, also failed to phase separate (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Phase separation was not observed when N122 (residues 1–122) was titrated with the rpL5 peptide.
source: Additionally, phase separation was not observed when an NPM1 construct containing only the OD (N122, residues 1–122; Figure 2a) was titrated with the rpL5 peptide (Figure 2c and Table 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2c and Table 2.

claim: The minimal multivalency requirements for phase separation are the acidic A1 and A2 tracts within NPM1 and at least two complementarily charged R-motifs within a polypeptide binding partner.
source: We thus conclude that the minimal multivalency requirements for phase separation are the acidic A1 and A2 tracts within NPM1 and at least two complementarily charged R-motifs within a polypeptide binding partner.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the experimental data.

claim: Fluorescence anisotropy (FA) of N130S125C labeled with Alexa Fluor594 within A2 increased in a biphasic manner upon titration of rpL5.
source: Fluorescence anisotropy (FA) of a N130S125C mutant, labeled with Alexa Fluor594 within A2, increased in a biphasic manner upon titration of rpL5 (Figure 3a).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3a.

claim: Monodisperse, soluble complexes formed at the first FA transition, which occurred at ~1:1 rpL5:N130 stoichiometry.
source: Results from small-angle neutron scattering (SANS) and analytical ultracentrifugation (AUC) experiments showed that monodisperse, soluble complexes formed at the first FA transition, which occurred at ~1:1 rpL5:N130 stoichiometry (Figure 3a, inset; Figure 3a–c; Figure 3—figure supplement 1; Table 3).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by multiple figures and Table 3.

claim: rpL5 bound to both the A1 and A2 tracts within 15N-N130 with a global KD of 57 ± 14 µM.
source: Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy showed that rpL5 bound to both the A1 and A2 tracts within 15N-N130 (Mitrea et al., 2014) with a global KD of 57 ± 14 µM (see Analysis methods) in agreement with isothermal titration calorimetry measurements (Table 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section, with reference to NMR data and Table 2.

claim: Residues within the A2 tract of apo N130 experienced fast, local motions with average local correlation time (τc,local) of 2.10 ± 0.05 ns and average local order parameter (Sf2) of 0.44 ± 0.01.
source: Residues within the A2 tract of the apo state, analyzed separately from the folded pentameric core (see Analysis methods), experienced fast, local motions [average local correlation time (τc,local), 2.10 ± 0.05 ns; average local order parameter (Sf2), 0.44 ± 0.01]; these motions were slowed when N130 was ~93% saturated with rpL5 (τc,local, 4.56 ± 0.06 ns; Table 5) and were reduced in amplitude (Sf2, 0.76 ± 0.01; Table 5).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on NMR relaxation data, with reference to Table 5.

claim: When N130 was ~93% saturated with rpL5, motions of A2 tract residues were slowed (τc,local, 4.56 ± 0.06 ns) and reduced in amplitude (Sf2, 0.76 ± 0.01).
source: Residues within the A2 tract of the apo state, analyzed separately from the folded pentameric core (see Analysis methods), experienced fast, local motions [average local correlation time (τc,local), 2.10 ± 0.05 ns; average local order parameter (Sf2), 0.44 ± 0.01]; these motions were slowed when N130 was ~93% saturated with rpL5 (τc,local, 4.56 ± 0.06 ns; Table 5) and were reduced in amplitude (Sf2, 0.76 ± 0.01; Table 5).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on NMR relaxation data, with reference to Table 5.

claim: A comparison of the overall tumbling time for core residues of N130 in the free and 93% rpL5 saturated state indicated 2:1 binding stoichiometry.
source: Furthermore, a comparison of the overall tumbling time for core residues of N130 in the free and 93% rpL5 saturated state indicated 2:1 binding stoichiometry (see Analysis methods).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on NMR analysis.

claim: The second transition in the FA curve (starting at ~2.5:1 rpL5:N130) corresponded to phase separation.
source: The second transition in the FA curve (starting at ~2.5:1 rpL5:N130) corresponded to phase separation (Figure 3a).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3a.

claim: The FRET efficiency (EFRET) for N130Q15C/S125C dually labeled with Alexa Fluor594 & 680 within the droplet phase (EFRET ~0.15) was dramatically reduced compared to that observed in the absence of rpL5 (EFRET ~0.85).
source: The FRET efficiency (EFRET) for this dye pair within the droplet phase (EFRET ~0.15) was dramatically reduced in comparison with that observed in the absence of rpL5 (EFRET ~0.85; Figure 5), consistent with the extension of the A2 tract from the N130 pentamer core due to interactions with rpL5 molecules upon phase separation (Figure 6a).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 5.

claim: The reduced FRET efficiency in the droplet phase is consistent with the extension of the A2 tract from the N130 pentamer core due to interactions with rpL5 molecules upon phase separation.
source: The FRET efficiency (EFRET) for this dye pair within the droplet phase (EFRET ~0.15) was dramatically reduced in comparison with that observed in the absence of rpL5 (EFRET ~0.85; Figure 5), consistent with the extension of the A2 tract from the N130 pentamer core due to interactions with rpL5 molecules upon phase separation (Figure 6a).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the FRET data, with reference to Figure 6a.

claim: The SANS curve for the 1:3 rpL5:N130 sample indicated periodic structural organization within the liquid-like droplets.
source: In contrast to the monodisperse character of the SANS curves for samples of rpL5 and N130 at 0:1 and 1:1 (rpL5:N130) stoichiometry (Figure 3b,c), the curve for the 1:3 sample indicated periodic structural organization within the liquid-like droplets (Figure 3b, red curve).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3b.

claim: The periodic structural organization in the 1:3 rpL5:N130 sample was interpreted in terms of inter-molecular correlation distances (55 Å, 77 Å, and 119 Å).
source: We interpreted these features in terms of inter-molecular correlation distances (55 Å, 77 Å, and 119 Å; see Analysis methods) due to organization of N130 and rpL5 induced by phase separation.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the SANS data.

claim: Nascent, higher order structural organization was evident in the SANS curve for a solution of rpL5 and N130 with 2:1 stoichiometry.
source: Notably, nascent, higher order structural organization was evident in the SANS curve for a solution of rpL5 and N130 with 2:1 stoichiometry (Figure 3b, green curve).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3b.

claim: Assembly of rpL5 and N130 into higher order, soluble intermediates at and above the 2:1 stoichiometric ratio was demonstrated using sedimentation velocity analytical ultracentrifugation (SV-AUC).
source: Assembly of rpL5 and N130 into higher order, soluble intermediates at and above the 2:1 stoichiometric ratio was also demonstrated using sedimentation velocity analytical ultracentrifugation (SV-AUC; Figure 3—figure supplement 1, Table 3).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3—figure supplement 1 and Table 3.

claim: Above the phase separation threshold (>3:1 rpL5:N130), resonances for residues within the N130 core broadened beyond detection in 2D 1H-15N TROSY spectra but not those for residues within the A2 tract.
source: Above the phase separation threshold (>3:1 rpL5:N130), resonances for residues within the N130 core broadened beyond detection in 2D 1H-15N TROSY spectra but not those for residues within the A2 tract (Figure 4a).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 4a.

claim: Chemical shift values indicated that residues within the A2 tract remained disordered in the phase separated state.
source: Chemical shift values indicated that these residues remained disordered.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on NMR chemical shift analysis.

claim: Upon saturation of the two principal binding sites within the A1 and A2 tracts on N130, bound rpL5 peptides extend toward and engage in weak interactions with neighboring N130 pentamers, creating 3D, expandable cross-links.
source: Upon saturation of the two principal binding sites within the A1 and A2 tracts on N130 (ii), bound rpL5 peptides extend toward and engage in weak interactions with neighboring N130 pentamers (iii), thus creating 3D, expandable cross-links.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as part of the proposed model, with reference to Figure 6b.

claim: The molecular basis of phase separation is the formation of non-covalent, inter-N130 pentamer interactions via the two R-motifs within the same rpL5 peptide molecule.
source: Together, our data support the hypothesis that the molecular basis of phase separation is the formation of non-covalent, inter-N130 pentamer interactions via the two R-motifs within the same rpL5 peptide molecule.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a hypothesis supported by the data.

claim: rpL5-mediated interactions establish the inter-pentamer spacing within the droplet phase that was detected by SANS.
source: We propose that these rpL5-mediated interactions establish the inter-pentamer spacing within the droplet phase that was detected by SANS (Figure 3b).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a proposal based on the SANS data.

claim: The phase separated sample formed between the peptide with the longer linker (rpL5-2xLinker) exhibited altered inter-molecular spacing, as indicated by altered correlation distances derived from the SANS curve.
source: The phase separated sample formed between the peptide with the longer linker (rpL5-2xLinker) exhibited altered inter-molecular spacing, as indicated by altered correlation distances derived from the SANS curve (Figure 7).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 7.

claim: The altered correlation distances with rpL5-2xLinker shifted to positions corresponding to larger correlation distances, in agreement with the hypothesis that the R-motif peptides establish inter-N130 pentamer spacing in the liquid-like phase.
source: These shifted to positions corresponding to larger correlation distances, in agreement with the hypothesis that the R-motif peptides establish inter-N130 pentamer spacing in the liquid-like phase.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as support for the proposed model.

claim: Both the OD and NBD are required for nucleolar localization of transfected NPM1.
source: However, both the OD (Enomoto et al., 2006; Jian et al., 2009) and NBD (Hisaoka et al., 2014; Negi and Olson, 2006) are required for nucleolar localization of transfected NPM1, suggesting that interactions with ribosomal RNA (rRNA) are also involved in integration of NPM1 within the GC matrix.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations to prior literature.

claim: Full length NPM1 (N294) exhibits a central intrinsically disordered region (IDR) that contains a longer acidic tract termed A3.
source: Full length NPM1 also exhibits a central intrinsically disordered region (IDR) that, in addition to the A2 tract, contains a longer acidic tract termed A3 (Figure 1a).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 1a.

claim: Full length NPM1 (N294) phase separates with either wheat germ rRNA or rpL5.
source: We tested and confirmed the ability of full length NPM1 (N294) to phase separate with either wheat germ rRNA or rpL5 using light scattering (Figure 8a & b, respectively) and fluorescence microscopy (Figure 9a, Rows 1 & 2, respectively).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figures 8 and 9.

claim: Binary mixtures of N294 with either rpL5 or rRNA formed droplets that increased in size over time.
source: Binary mixtures of N294 with either rpL5 or rRNA formed droplets that increased in size over time (Figure 9b); those with rpL5 fused more rapidly and were larger in size than those with rRNA.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 9b.

claim: Droplets of N294 with rpL5 fused more rapidly and were larger in size than those with rRNA.
source: Binary mixtures of N294 with either rpL5 or rRNA formed droplets that increased in size over time (Figure 9b); those with rpL5 fused more rapidly and were larger in size than those with rRNA.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 9b.

claim: Droplets of NPM1 with rpL5 formed at ~5-fold lower concentrations of both components than were required for phase separation with N130 and rpL5.
source: Furthermore, droplets of NPM1 with rpL5 formed at ~5-fold lower concentrations of both components (Figure 8b) than were required for phase separation with N130 and rpL5 (Figure 1b) due to the higher valency of acidic tracts within the full-length protein.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figures 8b and 1b.

claim: The lower concentration required for phase separation of N294 with rpL5 compared to N130 with rpL5 is due to the higher valency of acidic tracts within the full-length protein.
source: Furthermore, droplets of NPM1 with rpL5 formed at ~5-fold lower concentrations of both components (Figure 8b) than were required for phase separation with N130 and rpL5 (Figure 1b) due to the higher valency of acidic tracts within the full-length protein.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an explanation for the observed difference.

claim: rpL5 (and other R-motif peptides) and rRNA phase separated in the absence of N294, forming very small puncta.
source: Interestingly, rpL5 (and other R-motif peptides) and rRNA phase separated in the absence of N294 (Figure 8c,d), forming very small puncta (Figure 9a, Row 3).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figures 8c,d and 9a.

claim: When rpL5 was added to pre-formed droplets comprised of N294 and rRNA at a concentration below that which caused phase separation with N294 alone, the peptide accumulated into the rRNA/N294 droplets.
source: We next sought to understand the behavior of these three species in ternary mixtures by examining interactions between pre-formed droplets comprised of N294 and rRNA to which freely diffusing rpL5 was added, at a concentration below that which caused phase separation with N294 alone (Figure 9a, Row 4). The peptide accumulated into the rRNA/N294 droplets, highlighting NPM1's capacity to bind the two fundamental classes of macromolecules present in the nucleolus; these droplets also slowly grew over time (Figure 9b).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 9a and 9b.

claim: The accumulation of rpL5 into rRNA/N294 droplets highlights NPM1's capacity to bind the two fundamental classes of macromolecules present in the nucleolus.
source: The peptide accumulated into the rRNA/N294 droplets, highlighting NPM1's capacity to bind the two fundamental classes of macromolecules present in the nucleolus; these droplets also slowly grew over time (Figure 9b).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the experimental observation.

claim: Multi-modal binding by NPM1 mediates the co-assembly of rRNA and rpL5 within a dense, multi-component liquid-like phase.
source: Importantly, this multi-modal binding mediates the co-assembly of rRNA and rpL5 within a dense, multi-component liquid-like phase.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the ternary mixture experiments.

claim: The N240 construct (lacking the NBD) phase separated with rpL5.
source: In agreement with a mechanistic model wherein multivalent interactions between pentameric A1, A2, and A3 tracts within NPM1 and multivalent R-motifs within its nucleolar protein partners mediate phase separation, the N240, but not the ΔN construct phase separated with rpL5 (Figure 10a).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 10a.

claim: The ΔN construct (lacking the OD) did not phase separate with rpL5.
source: In agreement with a mechanistic model wherein multivalent interactions between pentameric A1, A2, and A3 tracts within NPM1 and multivalent R-motifs within its nucleolar protein partners mediate phase separation, the N240, but not the ΔN construct phase separated with rpL5 (Figure 10a).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 10a.

claim: Neither N240 nor ΔN constructs experienced phase separation in the presence of rRNA.
source: Furthermore, neither of these truncated constructs experienced phase separation in the presence of rRNA, confirming that multivalent display of the NBD is required for the co-localization of rRNA with NPM1 within liquid-like droplets (Figure 10b).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 10b.

claim: Multivalent display of the NBD is required for the co-localization of rRNA with NPM1 within liquid-like droplets.
source: Furthermore, neither of these truncated constructs experienced phase separation in the presence of rRNA, confirming that multivalent display of the NBD is required for the co-localization of rRNA with NPM1 within liquid-like droplets (Figure 10b).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the experimental data.

claim: Addition of N294 to pre-formed rpL5/rRNA puncta caused spontaneous formation of large droplets under conditions of both limiting and excess rpL5.
source: The addition of N294 to pre-formed, rpL5/rRNA puncta caused spontaneous formation of large droplets under conditions of both limiting and excess rpL5, whose sizes increased with increasing N294 concentration (Figure 11).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 11.

claim: Addition of the N240 deletion construct (lacking the NBD) to pre-formed rpL5/rRNA puncta caused phase separation under conditions of excess rpL5, but not with a limiting amount of rpL5.
source: In contrast, addition of the N240 deletion construct, lacking the NBD, caused phase separation under conditions of excess rpL5, but not with a limiting amount of rpL5 (Figure 11).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 11.

claim: Addition of the ΔN construct (lacking the OD) to pre-formed rpL5/rRNA puncta failed to cause phase separation under both excess and limiting rpL5 conditions.
source: Finally, addition of the ΔN construct, lacking the OD and therefore displaying dramatically reduced multivalency, failed to cause phase separation under both excess and limiting rpL5 conditions (Figure 11).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 11.

claim: The high valency associated with the NPM1 OD, together with the multiple acidic tracts and NBD, are required for the dissolution of rpL5/rRNA puncta and co-localization of these molecules within large liquid-like droplets.
source: Together, these results support a mechanism wherein the high valency associated with the NPM1 OD, together with the multiple acidic tracts and NBD, are required for the dissolution of rpL5/rRNA puncta and co-localization of these molecules within large liquid-like droplets that readily grow in size.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the experimental data.

claim: Through multi-modal interactions with two major classes of nucleolar macromolecules, NPM1 localizes to the nucleolus and mediates the co-localization of other protein-binding partners and rRNA within the GC of the nucleolus.
source: We thus propose that, through multi-modal interactions with two major classes of nucleolar macromolecules, NPM1 localizes to the nucleolus and also mediates the co-localization of other protein-binding partners and rRNA within the GC of the nucleolus.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a proposal based on the experimental findings.

claim: The eGFP-N294 fusion protein accumulated within purified nucleoli, even at sub-micromolar concentrations.
source: Consistent with in vitro results showing that all domains of NPM1 were required for the integration of both an R-motif peptide and rRNA into large, liquid-like droplets, the eGFP-N294 fusion protein accumulated within purified nucleoli, even at sub-micromolar concentrations (Figure 12b,c), while constructs lacking either the rRNA binding or oligomerization domains (eGFP-N240 or eGFP-△N, respectively) did not (Figure 12c).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 12b,c.

claim: Constructs lacking either the rRNA binding domain (eGFP-N240) or oligomerization domain (eGFP-△N) did not accumulate within purified nucleoli.
source: Consistent with in vitro results showing that all domains of NPM1 were required for the integration of both an R-motif peptide and rRNA into large, liquid-like droplets, the eGFP-N294 fusion protein accumulated within purified nucleoli, even at sub-micromolar concentrations (Figure 12b,c), while constructs lacking either the rRNA binding or oligomerization domains (eGFP-N240 or eGFP-△N, respectively) did not (Figure 12c).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 12c.

claim: The nucleolar localization of NPM1 requires multi-modal interactions with both R-motif-containing nucleolar proteins and rRNA.
source: These results suggested that the nucleolar localization of NPM1 requires multi-modal interactions with both R-motif-containing nucleolar proteins and rRNA.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the ex cellulo experiments.

claim: Full length mCherry-NPM1 accumulated in nucleoli and co-localized with the nucleolar markers NOPP140 and fibrillarin.
source: In agreement with the in vitro and ex cellulo results, full length mCherry-NPM1 accumulated in nucleoli and co-localized with the nucleolar markers NOPP140 (Figure 12d) and fibrillarin (Figure 12—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 12d and Figure 12—figure supplement 1.

claim: mCherry fluorescence was undetected in the mCherry-N240 cell lines.
source: Despite the fact that all cell lines expressed comparable levels of the Thy1.1 marker (Figure 12—figure supplement 2), and all NPM1 constructs encode the native bi-partite nuclear localization signal (residues 152–157 and 191–197 [Hingorani et al., 2000]), mCherry fluorescence was undetected in the mCherry-N240 cell lines, while the mCherry-ΔN cell lines exhibited diffuse mCherry fluorescence throughout the nucleus (Figure 12d and Figure 12—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 12d and Figure 12—figure supplement 1.

claim: The mCherry-ΔN cell lines exhibited diffuse mCherry fluorescence throughout the nucleus.
source: Despite the fact that all cell lines expressed comparable levels of the Thy1.1 marker (Figure 12—figure supplement 2), and all NPM1 constructs encode the native bi-partite nuclear localization signal (residues 152–157 and 191–197 [Hingorani et al., 2000]), mCherry fluorescence was undetected in the mCherry-N240 cell lines, while the mCherry-ΔN cell lines exhibited diffuse mCherry fluorescence throughout the nucleus (Figure 12d and Figure 12—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 12d and Figure 12—figure supplement 1.

claim: NPM1 mutants which lacked the ability to accumulate within nucleoli exhibited dramatically reduced half lives in cells.
source: Notably, Enomoto, et al., previously showed that NPM1 mutants which lacked the ability to accumulate within nucleoli exhibited dramatically reduced half lives in cells (Enomoto et al., 2006), a potential explanation for the undetectable levels of mCherry-N240 in our study.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citation to prior literature.

claim: Nucleolar localization of NPM1 is achieved only when interactions with both R-motif-containing nucleolar proteins and rRNA are possible.
source: Collectively, these data suggest that nucleolar localization of NPM1 is achieved only when interactions with both R-motif-containing nucleolar proteins and rRNA are possible.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the cell-based experiments.

claim: Deletion of either the NBD or OD abrogated the ability of NPM1 to simultaneously interact with an R-motif-containing peptide and rRNA within droplets in vitro.
source: Deletion of either the NBD or OD abrogated the ability of NPM1 to simultaneously interact with an R-motif-containing peptide and rRNA within droplets in vitro (Figure 11), suggesting that co-localization of NPM1 with the two types of nucleolar components in dense liquid-like droplets and localization within nucleoli arise through similar mechanisms involving multi-modal, multivalent interactions that promote phase separation.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 11.

claim: Co-localization of NPM1 with R-motif-containing proteins and rRNA in dense liquid-like droplets and localization within nucleoli arise through similar mechanisms involving multi-modal, multivalent interactions that promote phase separation.
source: Deletion of either the NBD or OD abrogated the ability of NPM1 to simultaneously interact with an R-motif-containing peptide and rRNA within droplets in vitro (Figure 11), suggesting that co-localization of NPM1 with the two types of nucleolar components in dense liquid-like droplets and localization within nucleoli arise through similar mechanisms involving multi-modal, multivalent interactions that promote phase separation.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the in vitro and cellular experiments.

claim: 83 (63%) of the proteins from the curated list of NPM1 interactors corresponded to those with predicted NoLSs.
source: Interestingly, 83 (63%) of the proteins from our curated list of NPM1 interactors corresponded to those with predicted NoLSs.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on comparison with a database of predicted NoLSs.

claim: Of the 83 NPM1 interactors with predicted NoLSs, 69 (83%) contained 2 or more R-motifs.
source: Of these 83, 69 (83%) contained 2 or more R-motifs, and there was extensive overlap between the sequence locations of the multivalent R-motifs that we identified and those of the predicted NoLSs (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on bioinformatics analysis.

claim: There was extensive overlap between the sequence locations of the multivalent R-motifs identified in this study and those of the predicted NoLSs.
source: Of these 83, 69 (83%) contained 2 or more R-motifs, and there was extensive overlap between the sequence locations of the multivalent R-motifs that we identified and those of the predicted NoLSs (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on bioinformatics analysis.

claim: Canonical NoLSs, which closely match the definition of multivalent R-motifs, enable proteins that are freely diffusing through the nuclear compartment to phase separate within the nucleolar matrix, thereby mediating their nucleolar localization.
source: Based on these observations, we propose that canonical NoLSs, which closely match our definition of multivalent R-motifs, enable proteins that are freely diffusing through the nuclear compartment to phase separate within the nucleolar matrix, thereby mediating their nucleolar localization.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a proposal based on the findings.

claim: More than 4,500 proteins are known to reside within the nucleolus.
source: Furthermore, while the NoLSs described by Scott, et al., account for the nucleolar localization of hundreds of proteins, more than 4,500 proteins are known to reside within the nucleolus (Ahmad et al., 2009), highlighting the need to identify additional localization mechanisms.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citation to prior literature.

claim: NPM1 does not exhibit a canonical NoLS.
source: Interestingly, along these lines, NPM1, although well established to be highly enriched in the nucleolus, does not exhibit a canonical NoLS.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an observation.

claim: Disruption of NPM1's multi-modal interactions, through abrogation of NBD oligomerization by deletion of the OD or removal of the NBD, hindered NPM1's ability to phase separate in vitro and to accumulate in nucleoli within mammalian cells.
source: In support of this, we found that disruption of its multi-modal interactions, through abrogation of NBD oligomerization by the deletion of the OD or removal of the NBD, hindered NPM1's ability to phase separate in vitro and to accumulate in nucleoli within mammalian cells (Figures 10–12).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by Figures 10-12.

claim: A previously described putative NoLS in NPM1 involves two buried Trp residues which are essential for proper folding of the NBD.
source: Consistent with our model, a previously described putative NoLS involves two buried Trp residues which are essential for proper folding of the NBD (Grummitt et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citation to prior literature.

claim: Mutations of the two buried Trp residues in the NBD destabilized the NBD, thereby impeding interactions with nucleic acids and nucleolar localization.
source: Mutations of these residues destabilized the NBD, thereby impeding interactions with nucleic acids and nucleolar localization (Banuelos et al., 2013; Chiarella et al., 2013; Falini et al., 2006; Grummitt et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations to prior literature.

claim: Multi-modal binding by NPM1 may play an important role in the structural organization of the nucleolus and the recruitment of proteins to the nucleolus.
source: Thus, we propose that multi-modal binding by NPM1 may play an important role in the structural organization of the nucleolus and the recruitment of proteins to the nucleolus.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a proposal based on the findings.

claim: Within the liquid-like matrix of the N130/rpL5 droplets, with diameters on the microns to tens of microns length scale, local ordering on the length scale of 5 to 12 nanometers was observed.
source: In our structural studies of the minimal phase separating system, N130/rpL5, we showed that within the liquid-like matrix of the droplets, with diameters on the microns to tens of microns length scale, we observed local ordering on the length scale of 5 to 12 nanometers (Figures 3 and 7).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by Figures 3 and 7.

claim: The intermolecular spacing indicated by SANS is dictated, at least in part, by the length of the linker connecting the two R-motifs in the divalent rpL5 peptide.
source: We propose that the intermolecular spacing indicated by SANS is dictated, at least in part, by the length of the linker connecting the two R-motifs in the divalent rpL5 peptide.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a proposal based on the SANS data.

claim: The 5-fold symmetry of the A1 binding grooves within the N130 pentamer is a factor in the spatial organization within the droplets.
source: Another factor in the spatial organization within these droplets is the 5-fold symmetry of the A1 binding grooves within the N130 pentamer that bind R-motifs within the rpL5 peptide (Figure 1 and [Mitrea et al., 2014]).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with reference to Figure 1 and prior work.

claim: The SANS data indicate the 'persistence length' of local structural order that provides 'structure' to the liquid-like droplets.
source: We suggest that the SANS data indicate the 'persistence length' of local structural order that, despite constant formation and dissociation of R-motif peptide-mediated cross-links, is sufficient to provide 'structure' to the liquid-like droplets.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an interpretation of the SANS data.

claim: The model for the structurally heterogenous integration of NPM1 within the nucleolar matrix provides a mechanistic explanation for its central role in many nucleolar functions, such as ribosome biogenesis and nucleolar stress responses.
source: This model for the the structurally heterogenous integration of NPM1 within the nucleolar matrix provides a mechanistic explanation for its central role in many nucleolar functions, such as ribosome biogenesis and nucleolar stress responses (Lindstrom, 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a conclusion from the proposed model.

claim: Three fundamental types of interactions mediated phase separation in the in vitro model system: (1) R-motifs binding to oligomeric, multivalent A-tracts, (2) low complexity multivalent R-motifs binding to rRNA, and (3) oligomeric, folded nucleic acid binding domains binding to rRNA.
source: Through studies of an in vitro model system based upon formation of multi-component liquid-like droplets, representing a simplified form of the GC of the nucleolus, we identified three fundamental types of interactions that mediated phase separation: (1) R-motifs (from nucleolar proteins) binding to oligomeric, multivalent A-tracts (within NPM1), (2) low complexity multivalent R-motifs binding to rRNA and (3) oligomeric, folded nucleic acid binding domains (within NPM1) binding to rRNA.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a summary of the findings.

claim: Disrupting either type (1) or (3) interactions abrogated accumulation of NPM1 within nucleoli.
source: Disrupting either type (1) or (3) interactions abrogated accumulation of NPM1 within nucleoli (Figure 12), demonstrating the relevance of our in vitro findings to the physiological setting.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by Figure 12.

claim: Complete loss of NPM1 from nucleoli did not preclude other nucleolar proteins (NOPP140 and fibrillarin) from accumulating within punctate nuclear structures.
source: Complete loss of NPM1 from nucleoli (e.g., in the Trp53-/-/Npm1-/- mouse embryonic fibroblasts cells) did not, however, preclude other nucleolar proteins (NOPP140 and fibrillarin; Figure 12 and Figure 12—figure supplement 1, respectively) from accumulating within punctate nuclear structures, in support of a model wherein collective interactions between many different nucleolar components drive their assembly into dense liquid-like structures.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by Figure 12 and Figure 12—figure supplement 1.

claim: Collective interactions between many different nucleolar components drive their assembly into dense liquid-like structures.
source: Complete loss of NPM1 from nucleoli (e.g., in the Trp53-/-/Npm1-/- mouse embryonic fibroblasts cells) did not, however, preclude other nucleolar proteins (NOPP140 and fibrillarin; Figure 12 and Figure 12—figure supplement 1, respectively) from accumulating within punctate nuclear structures, in support of a model wherein collective interactions between many different nucleolar components drive their assembly into dense liquid-like structures.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a conclusion from the observation in NPM1-null cells.

claim: The association of multivalency mediated by homo-oligomerization and acidic low complexity regions with phase separation is unique to NPM1.
source: Notably, the association of multivalency mediated by homo-oligomerization and acidic low complexity regions with phase separation is, to the best of our knowledge, unique to NPM1.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an observation about the uniqueness of NPM1's features.

claim: Similar features to those in NPM1 may be utilized by other proteins for incorporation into the nucleolar matrix.
source: We expect, however, that similar features may be utilized by other proteins for incorporation into the nucleolar matrix.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a speculation.

claim: NOPP140 exhibits 11 acidic, serine-rich clusters.
source: For example, NOPP140, known to be localized within the GC, exhibits 11 acidic, serine-rich clusters ([UniProt, 2014]; http://www.uniprot.org/uniprot/Q14978).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citation to the UniProt database.

claim: Nucleolin exhibits 3 acidic tracts (with lengths between 15 and 29 amino acids), 4 tandem folded RNA recognition motifs in addition to multivalent R-motifs.
source: Furthermore, nucleolin, which also lacks a canonical NoLS, exhibits 3 acidic tracts (with lengths between 15 and 29 amino acids), 4 tandem folded RNA recognition motifs in addition to multivalent R-motifs ([UniProt, 2014]; http://www.uniprot.org/uniprot/P19338), which may mediate multi-modal binding to protein and rRNA components within the dense liquid-like phase of the nucleolus.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citation to the UniProt database.

claim: The three fundamental types of interactions identified in this study mediate the localization of a wide variety of proteins, along with rRNA, within the liquid-like structure of the nucleolus.
source: We propose that the three fundamental types of interactions noted above mediate the localization of a wide veriety of proteins, along with rRNA, within the liquid-like structure of the nucleolus, providing new perspective on the term 'nucleolar localization signal'.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a proposal based on the findings.
